AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Ventilation-weighted Fourier decomposition-MRI (FD-MRI) has matured as a reliable technique for quantitative measures of regional lung ventilation in recent years, but has yet not been validated in COPD patients.

AbstractText.Label: PURPOSE/HYPOTHESIS
AbstractText.content: To compare regional fractional lung ventilation obtained by ventilation-weighted FD-MRI with dynamic fluorinated gas washout MRI (19 F-MRI) and lung function test parameters.

AbstractText.Label: POPULATION
AbstractText.content: Twenty-seven patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD, median age 61 [54-67] years) were included.

AbstractText.Label: FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE
AbstractText.content: For FD-MRI and for 19 F-MRI a spoiled gradient echo sequence was used at 1.5T.

AbstractText.Label: ASSESSMENT
AbstractText.content: FD-MRI coronal slices were acquired in free breathing. Dynamic 19 F-MRI was performed after inhalation of 25-30 L of a mixture of 79% fluorinated gas (C3 F8 ) and 21% oxygen via a closed face mask tubing using a dedicated coil tuned to 59.9 MHz. 19 F washout times in numbers of breaths (19 F-nbreaths ) as well as fractional ventilation maps for both methods (FD-FV, 19 F-FV) were calculated. Slices were matched using a landmark driven algorithm, and only corresponding slices with an overlap of >90% were coregistered for evaluation.

AbstractText.Label: STATISTICAL TESTS
AbstractText.content: The obtained parameters were correlated with each other using Spearman's correlation coefficient (r).

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: FD-FV strongly correlated with 19 F-nbreaths on a global (r = -0.72, P < 0.0001) as well as on a lobar level and with lung function test parameters (FD-FV vs. FEV1, r = 0.76, P < 0.0001). There was a small systematic overestimation of FD-FV compared to 19 F-FV (mean difference -0.03 (95% confidence interval [CI]: -0.097; -0.045).

AbstractText.Label: DATA CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Regional ventilation-weighted Fourier decomposition-MRI is a promising noninvasive, radiation-free tool for quantification of regional ventilation in COPD patients.

AbstractText.Label: LEVEL OF EVIDENCE
AbstractText.content: 2 Technical Efficacy: Stage 2 J. Magn. Reson. Imaging 2017.
